question: When does complete exact raw-product reuse beat the same uncached event?

environment.build_warnings: None reported by MSVC /W4 for the standalone worker

conditions.representation: Byte matrix indices decoded identically in U and M
conditions.PRNG: xorshift32 shifts 13,17,5; reset for each fixed scenario
conditions.M_key: Selected expert index and every input FP32 bit
conditions.key_counter_instrumentation_caveat: Timings include M key-comparison counters; incremental cost not isolated. No per-matrix-term counter instrumentation.
conditions.timed_scope: Entire event loop including router, key lookup/copies, decoding/matmul on misses, activation/state and output[0] checksum
conditions.excluded_timed_scope: Generation, VM construction/reset, correctness checks, final full-state hash, memory APIs, serialization and file I/O
conditions.calibration: U only; up to four intervals toward 50ms; whole 100-event cycles; cap100000 events or200million D*D terms
conditions.warmup: One excluded same-count interval per mode

validation.validation_only_gate: Two applicable tests passed; two post-timing/memory tests skipped
validation.preserved_RNL002_control: Seven data-only checks passed on existing results, including the rejected incomplete-key control; no new RNL002 worker execution

timing_assessments.counter_scope: Source-level counts, not CPU instructions; no per-term timed instrumentation

conclusion: Exact reuse reduced complete event time on fixed synthetic repeat-heavy inputs. Zero-repeat controls showed no gain; the cache retained additional memory. This does not establish a benefit for Revia language inference.
